chunks: He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Sulaiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said:

Among the admonitions given by Luqman to his son, he said to him: O my son, in your days, nights, and hours, keep a portion for yourself in seeking knowledge, for indeed you will never find any waste greater than abandoning it.

key_terms.تَضْيِيع: Waste, neglect — squandering of time or opportunity
key_terms.طَلَب الْعِلْم: Seeking knowledge — a fundamental obligation in Islam
key_terms.لُقْمَان: Luqman — the wise sage mentioned in Quran 31:12-19
key_terms.وَعَظَ: Admonished, gave counsel — moral and spiritual advice

ai.seo_question: What did Luqman advise his son about seeking knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) relates the wisdom of Luqman, the sage mentioned in the Quran (Surah 31), who advised his son to dedicate time every day and night to seeking knowledge. This hadith underscores that neglecting the pursuit of knowledge is the greatest waste one can commit, reflecting the centrality of learning in the Islamic tradition.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Ishfahani, from Sulaiman ibn Dawood al-Minqari, from Hammad ibn Isa, who reported that: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said:

Among the admonitions given by Luqman to his son, he said: "O son, in your days, night and hours, keep some portion for acquiring knowledge. Surely, you will not find any thing more wasteful than its disregard."
